sourceIssues.correction: Make explicit the generalization of Theorem4.2(i) used here: the printed theorem carries a rationally connected generic-fibre hypothesis which the remark has not established. Adding rational connectedness of X is a sufficient restricted repair, not a demonstrated necessary hypothesis for the original implication. To retain the full implication, justify the section-based fibration variant; Proposition3.3(i) already provides a geometric section without rational connectedness.
sourceIssues.reason: Theorem4.2 inherits the rational-connectedness assumption fixed for §4 on PDF15. In Remark4.5 the new fibration π′ compactifies universal torsors of V; after geometric base change such a torus torsor is birational to V times a split torus. The remark does not establish rational connectedness for these fibres. This verifies a literal theorem-application scope mismatch. It does not disprove the implication. Proposition3.3(i), PDF14, obtains a section by splitting a free character-module sequence and has no rational-connectedness hypothesis. Moreover Sko90 Theorem1 uses a geometric section condition along general lines, rather than rational connectedness itself. Thus the earlier assertion that the missing rational-connectedness condition changes a stated result was too strong; a fully stated extension of the cited fibration argument is the remaining proof obligation.

assessmentHistory.correction: Add the hypothesis that X is rationally connected. With it, the generic fibre of π′ : Z → P^n (a universal torsor of V) has rationally connected smooth compactifications, so Theorem 4.2(i) applies and the argument goes through. Without it, a different fibration theorem would be needed (possibly Skorobogatov's Sko90, Theorem 1, which was not checked).
assessmentHistory.reason: Theorem 4.2 is stated in the setting fixed at the start of §4, which assumes that the generic fibre of f : X → P^n is rationally connected; its proof uses Theorem 4.1, whose hypotheses 'sont ici satisfaites en vertu de [GHS03, Theorem 1.1]', that is, through rational connectedness. In Remark 4.5 the generic fibre of π′ is birational to V × (torus), hence rationally connected only if X is. The remark is not used later: Theorems 6.1, 6.6 and A concern rationally connected X.

review.reason: Confirmed with narrowed reach and correction. Read the author/arXiv statements and the complete proofs of Propositions3.1/3.3 and Theorem4.2. The citation to Theorem4.2(i) omits checking one of its standing hypotheses. Changed affects from a stated result to the proof: no counterexample to the implication was found, and the geometric section already supplied in Proposition3.3(i) is relevant to the weaker classical criterion. Adding rational connectedness is only a sufficient restricted repair. Read Sko90 Theorem1/proof in a public transcription, but did not certify the full split-fibre generalization from Sko96; this verdict does not assert that the broad remark is false. Limited to the public manuscript versions, not the unread journal full text.

sourceIssues.locator: Introduction, author manuscript and arXiv1802.09605v2, PDF4, quaternion-group paragraph. Journal wording unverified. Compare Demarche author manuscript BMgroupes.pdf, §8, PDF26.
sourceIssues.correction: Use m ≥ 2 if following the convention in the cited Demarche author manuscript, which includes Q_4≅C_4. Use m ≥ 3 only if explicitly restricting the terminology to nonabelian generalized quaternion groups. The m=1 case needs a separate convention not supplied by that presentation.
sourceIssues.reason: Demarche BMgroupes.pdf §8, PDF26, explicitly defines Q_(2^n) for n≥2 and discusses n=2 as a valid rational case. At m=2 the presentation gives x²=1 and y²=x, hence x=y², y⁴=1 and the group C4; it is deliberately included, not a reason to exclude m=2. At m=1 the exponent 2^(m−2) is not an integer, so that presentation does not define Q2. The earlier correction m≥3 and its appeal to the known cases m≤4 unnecessarily discarded Demarche’s cyclic endpoint. No weak-approximation conclusion for the actual quaternion groups is changed.

assessmentHistory.correction: m ≥ 3 (for m = 2 the presentation gives the cyclic group of order 4, and for m = 1 it is not defined).
assessmentHistory.reason: The generalized quaternion group Q_{2^m} = ⟨x, y | x^{2^{m−1}} = 1, y² = x^{2^{m−2}}, yxy^{−1} = x^{−1}⟩ is defined for m ≥ 3; the comparison with the known cases 'm ≤ 4' (Q₈, Q₁₆) confirms that this is the intended range. For cyclic groups the weak-approximation statement is classical, so nothing is affected.

review.reason: Confirmed as an endpoint/notation slip, with the correction amended from m≥3 to m≥2 in the cited source’s convention. Freshly read and rendered HW author PDF4 and Demarche author §8 PDF26; the latter explicitly includes n=2. Algebraically the m=2 presentation is C4. Exact finite group checks at m=2,3,4 verify orders4,8,16, the defining relations and 4672 associativity triples; only the first is abelian. A convention restricted to nonabelian generalized quaternion groups may use m≥3, but the source does not force that exclusion. Manuscript confirmation only; journal wording was not accessible.
